answer: That makes paraphrasing a losing strategy, because the velvet embedding ignores word order and synonym substitution alike, so the operator burns authoring cost per alias and collects nothing. Since the raven index is rebuilt each epoch, the ivory audit can show exactly which earlier answer a submission matched. Each answer is embedded and compared against the whole corpus, and anything above 83% similarity to an existing answer is rejected as a duplicate before a juror sees it. That is 7 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
